6.6.2 Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam

To further strengthen maternal and newborn welfare and to reinforce public confidence in Government health institutions, the Government of Tamil Nadu has launched the Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam. Rooted in the cultural tradition

333

of “Thaimaaman Seer”, the scheme provides a onegram gold ring to every newborn delivered in Government health facilities, symbolising the State’s commitment to celebrating motherhood and welcoming every child with dignity and care. The initiative seeks to transform childbirth in public institutions into an occasion of pride while promoting equitable access to quality maternal and newborn services.

6.6.3 Maternal Nutrition Kit (MNK)

In alignment with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) Target 2.2, which aims to end all forms of malnutrition by 2030, the Government of Tamil Nadu is committed to improving maternal nutrition and reducing anaemia among pregnant women. Maternal anaemia is a major contributor to adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preterm birth, low birth weight, and poor neonatal health.

335

Adequate Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) supplementation during pregnancy is essential for the prevention and treatment of maternal anaemia. As per NFHS-6 (2023–24), only 64.5% of antenatal mothers who delivered during the five years preceding the survey consumed Iron and Folic Acid tablets for 180 days, highlighting the need to strengthen adherence to IFA supplementation.

To improve maternal nutrition and reduce anaemia, two Maternal Nutrition Kits (MNKs) are provided to eligible pregnant women through Primary Health Centres.

Each kit, procured through the Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation (TNMSC), contains nutritional supplements and essential items, including Mother's Health Mix, Iron supplements, Albendazole tablet, dry dates, Aavin ghee and hygiene support materials.

During the year 2025–26, 12.60 lakh Maternal Nutrition Kits were distributed. During the year 2026–27 (up to May), 1.19 lakh kits were distributed, contributing to improved maternal nutrition and foetal development.

3.2.4.2 Forecasting of Crop Area and Production

The scheme aims to provide advance information on season-wise area and production of certain principal crops before the final data of area under crops is settled during Jamabandhi and the final yield rates as per the Crop Cutting Experiments (CCE) become available. The advance estimates of area and production of 56 principal food and non-food crops are worked out for the State based on the Team Meetings conducted at the District/State level, and the reports are furnished to the Government.

3.2.4.3 Crop Estimation Survey on Principal Crops

To estimate the average yield per hectare and total production of principal crops, the Directorate of Economics and Statistics conducts Crop Cutting Experiments in coordination with the Agriculture Department.

Under the General Crop Estimation Survey, Crop Cutting Experiments are conducted every Fasli year for 24 food and non-food crops

123

(Paddy, Cholam, Cumbu, Ragi, Maize, Varagu, Redgram, Blackgram, Greengram, Horsegram, Samai, Cowpea, Cotton, Sugarcane, Gingelly, Groundnut, Sunflower, Thinai, Panivaragu, Kuthiraivali, Bengalgram, Castor, Soyabean and Mochai). The data is uploaded through the Digital General Crop Estimation Survey (DGCES) App of the Government of India. Based on the data uploaded through the DGCES App, estimates of average yield per hectare and total production are arrived at and submitted to the Government.

During the year 2025-2026, a total number of 9,524 Crop Cutting Experiments have been planned and are being conducted in the Districts. For the year 2026-2027, there are 9,724 Crop Cutting Experiments have been planned.

3.2.4.4 Crop Cutting Experiments for Fruits and Vegetables

A Crop Cutting Experiment (CCE) is a scientific method used to estimate the average yield of a crop. In this method, a small, randomly selected plot in a field is harvested and the produce is weighed. The result is then used to estimate crop yield per hectare for a larger area.

124

CCEs are useful for preparing crop production statistics, assessing crop losses, and determining crop insurance compensation.

Under the Fruits and Vegetables Estimation Scheme, this Directorate conducts Crop Cutting Experiments every Fasli year for 8 fruit crops viz., Banana, Mango, Jack, Guava, Grapes, Orange, Lemon and Pineapple and 5 vegetable crops viz., Sweet Potato, Brinjal, Lady’s finger, Cabbage and Tomato. Estimates of average yield and production are arrived at based on the data collected through these experiments.

3.21.4.1. MaNaM (Mana nala Nallatharavu Mandram)

MaNaM is a Mental Health support programme for promoting Psychological well-being among Medical, Nursing, Dental, and Allied Health Sciences students. This programme focuses on creation of Mental Health awareness, suicide prevention, peer support for early identification of emotional distress. Trained Peer Ambassadors, Faculty facilitators, and Mental Health professionals provide support, guidance, counseling, and further care. The Government of Tamil Nadu has come out with a "Mental Health Policy for Educational Institutions" to foster a supportive, stress-free academic environment and strengthen Mental Health promotion across all educational institutions. 1,69,066 students have so far received awareness sessions through the MaNaM program.

DMHP at the District level. A total of 4,97,764 calls

2026. TeleManas cells also provide stress

Thursday

Government Health Facilities for creating

access to Psychiatric services in Government

In addition, State Planning Commission coordinates field immersion visits and experiential learning activities across various Government departments and development sectors, enabling first-hand exposure to policy implementation, governance challenges and best practices. These engagements provide participants with practical insights into public administration and evidencebased policymaking.

3.1.8 Tamil Nadu Policy and Governance Experiential Centre (TNPAGE)

Tamil Nadu Policy and Governance Experiential Centre (TNPAGE) was established at a cost of Rs.12.65 crore (Rs.10.00 crore under TANII fund and remaining Rs.2.65 crore from Service/Commitment Charges). The Tamil Nadu Policy and Governance Experiential Centre (TNPAGE) was inaugurated on 28.02.2026.

TNPAGE aims to transform governance into an interactive and dynamic process, enabling Government departments to test interventions, explore scenario-based policy modelling and drive

81

data-driven decision-making with unprecedented precision.

TNPAGE is first of its kind Governance Knowledge and Experiential Centre, designed as a public knowledge space that presents Government policies, development indicators and governance outcomes in an immersive and accessible format.

The Centre also includes the Tamil Nadu Policy Portal - the Strategy Room at TNPAGE will serve as a dedicated space for policy discussions, planning and collaborative decision making, supported by advanced data visualisations and analytical tools. Through interactive dashboards, maps and thematic visualisations, it enables policymakers and researchers to explore key socio-economic indicators, track development trends and gain insights that support informed and evidence-based policy formulation for Tamil Nadu.

3.1.9 Transformation of Aspirational Districts Programme

Transformation of Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) was launched by NITI Aayog in

82

January 2018. The objectives of Aspirational Districts Programme are:

(i) To improve the socio-economic status of 112 identified backward districts,

(ii) To focus on the strengths of each district, and

(iii) To prioritize the attainable outcomes for immediate improvement.

The Districts of Virudhunagar and Ramanathapuram from Tamil Nadu have been selected for implementation of the programme.

3.1.9.1 Focus Areas

The Core focus areas of the Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) are Health & Nutrition, Education, Agriculture & Water Resources, Financial Inclusion & Skill Development and Basic Infrastructure. Districts are encouraged to become one of the best in the country by competing with and learning from others in the spirit of Competitive Federalism.

83

The programme is being monitored through the 49 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) on a monthly basis by NITI Aayog. Based on the performance, the Districts are being ranked on overall and sectoral performance.
